H.R. 1346 (119th Congress) - Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act of 2025, Engrossed in House text

notes: First-refresh audit, 2026-09-01. Removed outright (contradicted or unsourceable): the cosponsor count of 54 (it is 55, 37 R / 18 D); "opposition from petroleum industry interests, some environmental groups concerned about ... life-cycle emissions, and procedural challenges in scheduling a standalone vote" (invented - replaced with the recorded floor record: a closed rule, a failed motion to recommit, a 218-203 roll call); "EPA has granted limited emergency E15 waivers in specific years when corn ethanol supply was high and gasoline prices were elevated" (contradicted by EPA own waiver log - seven chained waivers covered the whole 2025 season and a nationwide waiver was live on 2026-08-20); "roughly 96% by age"; "first approved for use in model year 2001 and newer vehicles"; the E15-sells-at-a-discount / market-expansion paragraph; "has passed the House multiple times in previous Congresses"; and the 1990 rationale about carbon monoxide and particulates. The 1.0 psi mechanism, absent from the bill text (grep: zero psi figures), is now sourced where it actually lives - 42 U.S.C. 7545(h)(4) and EPA own RVP page - and the bill is described by what it does: strike "10 percent" and insert "10 to 15 percent". Added: the small-refining-company / RFS half of the bill, which cache.json had flagged UNDERREPORTED and the article omitted entirely; and the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 cross-reference that the engrossed text carries. SIGN-OFF ROUND (round 2) fixes: the 2016-2018 credit-return bullet silently dropped the 2018 cohort ALTERNATIVE denied-petition condition (211(o)(9)(F)(iii)(III)(bb)) and every December 1, 2022 anchor - rewritten in full; the "Summarising 40 CFR 1090.215" framing was wrong (the season quotes come from EPA opening paragraph, not from its 1090.215 summary) - replaced with the sourced December 4, 2020 relocation plus EPA own two season sentences; the JSON-LD description and about.name presented the DROPPED short title as the current name, contradicting the article own note-on-the-name paragraph - both now carry the official title; "four more" states overclaimed EPA e.g./include list - now "among"; "each running about three weeks" replaced with the counted 20-day spans; "most of the text" replaced with the subsection count (5 of 7); and two unsourced comparatives ("easy to miss", "the 2026 season went further") were removed. Added on the same round: the clause (ii) no-subsequent-redesignation limit on the 75 percent cut, and the section 1(c)(2) savings provision - both real limits the bullets had stated without. FROZEN-TEXT SONNET ROUND (round 3) returned 5 BLOCKING, all dropped statutory conditions in the RFS bullets, all confirmed on an independent read of the engrossed text and all fixed: (1) the small-refining-company threshold is counted only "across all of the facilities of the company, entity, or group of affiliated entities that produced transportation fuel subject to the requirements of paragraph (2)", not across every facility the group owns; (2) the exemption-termination bullet omitted clause (cc), the Administrator "not later than October 1, 2028" deadline to act on outstanding petitions; (3) the closure-risk exemption omitted its "not later than December 31 of a calendar year" filing deadline; (4) it implied the senior-officer attestation alone backs the petition, when clause (H)(ii)(I) also requires demonstrating imminent risk, that the risk is "solely caused by the cost of compliance", and unchanged ownership, and clause (v) lets the Administrator grant it "only upon a determination" that BOTH are met; (5) "qualifying small refinery" was used but never defined - now carries the (H)(viii) definition (prior paragraph (9) extension, OR crude throughput not exceeding 10,000 barrels AND production begun on or after January 1, 2007 and before January 1, 2026). Two of that round advisories were also applied: the no-reallocation rule scope clause ("For the purpose of making the determinations in paragraph (2)(B)(ii)") and the returned-credits rider ("notwithstanding paragraph (5)(C), deemed eligible for future compliance years"). Declined with reason: the paragraph (4) "Provided, however" proviso (the article does not claim to quote the whole paragraph, and the bill only strikes the lead-in words); the title date-ambiguity and the "for Gas Stations" hook (pre-existing title, and the body first line states the May 13, 2026 passage date); the dateModified/September-2026 mismatch (resolved by this refresh publish). CONVERGENCE ROUND (round 4, frozen text, fresh Sonnet) found a SIXTH dropped condition the earlier round had missed: clause (H)(vi) Scope and duration, which limits a granted exemption to "in whole or in part", "only ... to the extent necessary to prevent the closure, permanent idling, or conversion", and "only ... with respect to the calendar year for which the petition for the exemption is submitted" - confirmed on an independent read and added. Its advisory on the volume cap was also applied: the 2028 cap is a volume of ALL renewable fuel whose energy content equals that of 150 million gallons of conventional biofuel, and later years are adjusted in direct proportion - both now stated. SIGN-OFF ROUND (round 5, frozen text, fresh Sonnet, exhaustive clause-by-clause) returned 0 BLOCKING and found NO further dropped or mis-nested condition anywhere in Section 1(b)-(g). Two of its four advisories applied, both the same dropped-qualifier-inside-a-quote class: the substantially-similar test in the new 211(f)(4)(C) was quoted without its "pursuant to paragraph (1)(A)" cross-reference, and the qualifying-small-refinery throughput test was glossed as "average daily crude oil throughput" when the statute says "average aggregate daily crude oil throughput for a calendar year" and supplies the averaging method - both now carried in full. Two declined with reason: (a) the 75-percent clause is quoted from "reduce" onward and deliberately omits "subject to clause (ii)", because the very next sentence states clause (ii) in full and quotes it, so the condition is carried rather than dropped; (b) "sold year-round" is not synthesis - the bill own operative section is headed "YEAR-ROUND E15 AND RFS REFORM" and a ledger row binds the phrase to that heading.
